subject: What Changed to Your Credit Card Today? Edition 10
summary: The Pine Labs HDFC Bank Pro Credit Card is discontinued, the third Pine Labs or HDFC co-branded card to lose new-applicant status this week.
body_html:
A quiet day, one change, and it's a small but tidy bookend to a story we've been tracking all week: HDFC's Pine Labs co-branded cards.

Pine Labs HDFC Bank Pro Credit Card

This card is now marked discontinued and closed to new applications. That makes it the third Pine Labs or HDFC co-branded card to lose new-applicant status this week, after the Pine Labs HDFC Bank Credit Card and the Retailio HDFC Bank Credit Card were both discontinued on 28 August. HDFC's standard language applies here too: existing cardholders keep every current feature and benefit until they're migrated to a replacement card, whether that happens at reissuance, replacement, or renewal.

The catch: "unaffected for now" is doing a lot of work in that sentence. It holds until your card comes up for renewal or reissue, at which point you get migrated to whatever HDFC decides is the replacement, not necessarily on your terms.

What I'd actually do with this

If you hold the Pine Labs HDFC Bank Pro Credit Card, there's nothing to act on today. Your card works exactly as it did yesterday. But given this is now the third card in this specific co-branded family to get discontinued in a week, it's a reasonable bet that HDFC is winding down the whole Pine Labs partnership rather than making isolated product decisions. When your migration notice arrives, read the replacement card's terms closely before assuming it's a like-for-like swap, ask specifically what happens to your existing reward points balance and whether the new card's fee structure matches what you're paying now.

This is my honest read, not formal financial advice. I'm not your advisor, and before you make a call on any of this, run it past a professional or at least sleep on it. But this is exactly how I'd think about it if it were my card.

Monzy
